capex_to_revenue.why: Capital spending has fallen after the large manufacturing build-out: 2026 nine-month capex is 1.4% of revenue and 2025 was 2.1%, against a 3.5% five-year pooled figure. I use 2.5% to allow for maintenance and some suite expansion.

fade_years.why: Patent protection extends well beyond the five-year forecast, so margin and growth normalize gradually; 10 years is a moderate fade.

long_run_op_margin.why: Non-GAAP gross margin is 77-79% with SG&A that is 43% of revenue on a non-GAAP basis. The GAAP margin carries stock compensation and $57.3M of annual amortization, and the acquired intangibles have 9-14 year lives, so the amortization drag eventually fades. About 15% is a mid-case between the leverage upside and the risks from generics and the royalty.

op_margin.why: Nine-month 2026 operating income is about 6% of revenue, helped by lower SG&A in Q3 and by other operating gains. Margin rises as SG&A leverage builds, manufacturing yields improve and amortization falls with the divestiture. A possible RDF royalty and the cost of defending patents against generics cap the gains.

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The company is asset-light apart from manufacturing, and the base-year return on tangible capital is 13.5%, well above the 7.4% break-even. I use about that level, trimmed for competition.

rev_growth.why: Year 1 is about 2%: guidance of $735-760M for 2026 (before withdrawal) compares with $726.4M in 2025, and the nine months are up 3% but Q3 slipped. Growth in 2027 is held down by losing about $24M of iovera° revenue after the divestiture. After that, EXPAREL volume and separate reimbursement support about 4-4.5%, offset by price erosion, flat ZILRETTA and generic risk.

quotes.quote: all with an expiration date between January 2041 and July 2044

terminal_growth.why: A concentrated specialty pharma franchise protected by EXPAREL patents into 2041-2044 can grow near nominal GDP. I set it below the 3.75% anchor because of single-product concentration and generic challenges.

risks.risk: Generic EXPAREL entry or patent loss (WhiteOak and Qilu ANDAs) hits the product that is 79% of revenue.
The RDF royalty is reinstated on EXPAREL made at 200-liter scale, while litigation and SG&A costs stay high, so margins stay compressed.
The Viatris deal fails and the standalone business loses momentum and competes with new non-opioid analgesics, which lowers the long-term growth rate.

The pending Viatris deal at $36.50 per share withdrew management guidance, so the forecast is a standalone view.

business_model.claim: Pacira sells non-opioid pain products: EXPAREL, a long-acting local analgesic for postsurgical pain, ZILRETTA, an extended-release knee osteoarthritis injection, and until July 2026 the iovera° cryoanalgesia device. It also has pipeline programs, led by the PCRX-201 gene therapy for knee osteoarthritis.

business_model.claim: EXPAREL is the flagship and dominant revenue source: $575.1 million of 2025 net product sales, 79% of 2025 total revenues.
quotes: During 2025, sales of EXPAREL accounted for 79% of our total revenue, and we expect EXPAREL sales will remain of primary importance for the foreseeable future.

business_model.claim: ZILRETTA is the second product, $116.6 million or 16% of 2025 revenue. It is sold through a physician 'buy and bill' model.
quotes: ZILRETTA is a physician-administered product, and therefore physicians are required to purchase and manage the inventory of ZILRETTA, prior to administering the product to patients.

quotes: We drop-ship EXPAREL directly to end-users based on orders placed to wholesalers or directly to us, and there is no product held by wholesalers.
secure formulary approvals for EXPAREL at a substantial number of targeted hospitals and ASCs

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: EXPAREL is the main revenue driver. It was 79% of 2025 total revenue, and its revenue rose 5% in 2025 on a 6% increase in gross vial volume. For this to continue, volume growth has to keep outpacing price erosion.
quotes: During 2025, sales of EXPAREL accounted for 79% of our total revenue
EXPAREL revenue increased 5% in 2025 versus 2024.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q2 2026 earnings release; the mechanism is inferred from the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Broader payer reimbursement for EXPAREL is a stated enabler of use. The NOPAIN Act took effect in January 2025, and UnitedHealthcare now reimburses EXPAREL separately outside the surgical bundle. Growth from this depends on more payers and sites of care adopting separate reimbursement.
quotes: This update enables EXPAREL to be reimbursed outside of the surgical bundle for eligible UnitedHealthcare members, representing an additional step in expanding access to non-opioid postsurgical pain management options.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and 10-Q MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Partnerships are adding geographic reach for EXPAREL. LG Chem has Asia-Pacific rights and paid a $2.0 million upfront. Molteni has European rights, with a first commercial sale expected in 2027. Continued growth depends on partners obtaining regulatory approvals and launching.
quotes: Through this partnership, LG Chem has the exclusive rights to commercialize EXPAREL for postsurgical pain management in the region.
The first commercial sale is currently expected to occur in 2027.

growth_thesis.basis: Target and 2025 results stated in the 10-K; 2026 trend is not stated.
growth_thesis.claim: Margin expansion through manufacturing efficiency is a stated growth lever. Gross margin was 79% in 2025 versus 76% in 2024, and the 5x30 plan targets a further gross-margin improvement. It requires the larger-scale EXPAREL manufacturing suites to deliver lower cost per unit.
quotes: achieve a five percentage-point improvement in gross margins over 2024

growth_thesis.claim: Reported profit growth in 2026 is large but helped by non-operating and one-time items. Nine-month net income was 36,090 versus 5,397 (statement in thousands of USD). Income from operations was 33,441 versus 16,851, with third-quarter SG&A of 83,840 versus 91,797. For the improvement to be durable, it must come from lower SG&A and not from gains.

growth_thesis.basis: Inferred from the 10-Q cash flow and income statements.
growth_thesis.claim: Cash generation and share repurchases are lifting per-share results. Nine-month operating cash flow was 133,210 versus 108,305 (statement in thousands of USD). Treasury purchases were 50,045, and diluted weighted shares were 40,681 versus 45,729 (shares in thousands). Continued per-share growth requires sustained operating cash flow.

ZILRETTA is a secondary, flatter contributor. Revenue fell 1% in 2025 on a 4% drop in kit volume, partly offset by a 3% price gain. A July 2025 co-promotion with J&J MedTech is intended to support it. Growth requires kit volume to recover against inexpensive generic steroids.
quotes: ZILRETTA revenue decreased 1% in 2025 versus 2024, primarily due to a 4% decrease in kit volume, partially offset by a 3% increase in net selling price per unit.

growth_thesis.basis: Program status stated in the 10-Q; the spending is from the 10-Q income statement.
growth_thesis.claim: The pipeline (PCRX-201 and PCRX-2002, both Phase 2) is a future growth option with no revenue yet. Nine-month R&D was 84,997 versus 79,859 (statement in thousands of USD). Growth from it requires clinical success and eventual approval.
quotes: We are also advancing two Phase 2 clinical programs

growth_thesis.basis: Divestiture terms stated in the earnings release and 10-Q; the revenue effect is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Selling iovera° trades a small growing product line for cash and a share of future milestones, so EXPAREL and ZILRETTA must carry growth. The sale closed on July 31, 2026 for cash of $73.6 million, with up to an additional $70 million in revenue-based milestones possible. iovera° grew 6% in 2025.
quotes: The transaction closed on July 31, 2026 and the Company received cash of $73.6 million, after purchase price adjustments.

growth_thesis.claim: EXPAREL's growth depends on keeping its patent protection and its cost structure. The company lists 23 EXPAREL patents in the Orange Book, expiring between January 2041 and July 2044. Two Chinese generic filers have challenged EXPAREL, and a November 2026 appeals ruling now requires royalties on the larger-scale process.
quotes: With these two new patents, there are currently 23 EXPAREL patents listed in the Orange Book, all with an expiration date between January 2041 and July 2044.

On November 6, 2026, the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit reversed the District Court’s judgment in part, holding that the Company owes royalties on EXPAREL manufactured using its 200-liter process and directing the District Court to enter judgement in favor of RDF on that claim.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 8-Ks, the 10-Q and the screener row.
growth_thesis.claim: The pending Viatris acquisition conditions the whole standalone growth case. Viatris has offered $36.50 per share in cash, and the screener price is 36.48. The company has withdrawn its 2026 guidance, so management's own growth outlook is not available.
quotes: In addition, the Company is withdrawing its previously issued 2026 financial guidance and will not provide further updates to such guidance during the pendency of the proposed Offer and Merger.
